founded.what: The year a wine business at Reims is first recorded, the house that took the name Louis Roederer in 1833.

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, in the trade's own word, though it farms an unusually high share of its own fruit for a house; Cristal comes from its own vineyards alone.

story: The house that became Louis Roederer was a Reims wine business recorded in 1776. A nephew of its owner inherited it in 1833 and gave it his own name, and under him and his son the house sold widely in Russia. In 1876 Tsar Alexander II (1818 to 1881) asked the house to set aside a cuvée for his court each year, and it was bottled in clear glass with a flat base so that, as the story is told, nothing could be hidden in the bottle or its punt. The revolution of 1917 ended the imperial orders and much of the Russian trade. From 1932 a widow of the family led the house for more than forty years, by its own account through its hardest times, and in 1945, by two accounts, Cristal was first sold to the public. A rosé followed with the 1974 harvest, and in the 1970s her grandson took over. On 5 July 1993 Louis Roederer took sixty per cent of Deutz, at Aÿ. Unlike most houses, Roederer built its prestige wine on its own vineyards, and Cristal 2012 was the first made wholly from biodynamically farmed vines. The house marked its two hundred and fiftieth year in 2026.

style.line: Ripe estate fruit held on a tight line, a share of the wine aged in oak casks and a low dosage: a house that tastes like a domaine, as the library puts it, built on its own vineyards.
style.grapes: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay lead, with Meunier in Collection; Cristal comes only from the house's own Grand Cru vineyards on the Montagne de Reims, at Aÿ and in the Côte des Blancs.
style.vessels: A share in oak: a quarter of Cristal 2015 was fermented or aged in oak casks, by the house's sheet.
style.malolactic: Blocked for Cristal 2015, to keep the fruit bright, fresh and pure, by the house; usually blocked for Cristal, by its sheets.
style.lees: Six to seven years on its lattes for Cristal 2015, then six to twelve months more after disgorging, by the house.
style.dosage: 7 grams a litre for Cristal 2015, by the house's sheet.

nv.name: Collection
nv.note: The multi vintage Brut, numbered by the house's count of its harvests, Collection 242 the first, which replaced Brut Premier.

cuvee.name: Cristal

first.what: The year Cristal was first made, for the court of Tsar Alexander II; it was first sold to the public in 1945, by two accounts.

cuvee.rhythm: Made for the Tsar's court from 1876 and sold to the public from 1945, by more than one account, in the years the house declares; the 2008, 2012, 2014 and 2015 are among the vintages sold.
cuvee.blend: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, in shares that change with the year: about three fifths Pinot Noir in 2015 by the house's sheet; no Meunier.
cuvee.sites: Only the house's own Grand Cru vineyards: Verzenay, Verzy and Beaumont-sur-Vesle on the Montagne de Reims, Aÿ in the Marne valley, and Avize, Cramant and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger in the Côte des Blancs; 45 plots in the seven crus for the 2015.
cuvee.making: Estate parcels are vinified apart, a quarter of them in oak casks for the 2015, with the malolactic conversion blocked to keep its tension. The wine rests six to seven years on its lattes in the Reims cellars and six to twelve months more after disgorging, with a dosage of 7 grams a litre for the 2015, by the house.
cuvee.lees: Six to seven years on its lattes for the 2015, by the house, about six years in the published record.
cuvee.bottle: Clear glass with a flat base, first made for the Tsar's court in 1876: as the story is told, so nothing could be hidden in the bottle or its punt. The coloured cellophane round each bottle keeps light from a wine in clear glass.
cuvee.young: Meyer lemon, white peach and fresh almond over crushed chalk, with a delicate, creamy mousse and a taut, saline line.
cuvee.aged: Time brings toasted brioche, hazelnut and honeyed pastry while the line stays taut; the house's late release of the 2008 adds candied lemon, almond, wheat and cocoa.

forms.name: Cristal Rosé
forms.note: The rosé of a declared year, first made with the 1974 harvest, in far smaller quantity.

forms.name: Cristal Vinothèque
forms.note: Cristal held back in the house's cellars for some twenty years before a late release, by the house's sheet for the 1995.

cuvee.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass, the cellophane left on until the bottle is opened.

table.house45: Louis Roederer's story begins at Reims in 1776, and the house took its name in 1833. In the nineteenth century it sold widely in Russia, and in 1876 Tsar Alexander the Second asked for a cuvée of his own, in clear glass. That wine is Cristal. Unlike most houses, Roederer farms much of its own fruit and makes Cristal from its own Grand Cru vineyards alone. The style is ripe fruit kept tight and fresh, with a share aged in oak casks and little added sugar. Guests know the house first by Collection, its non vintage, and above all by Cristal, its prestige cuvée.
table.house10: Louis Roederer is the Reims house, dated from 1776, that farms its own vineyards and made Cristal for the Tsar.
table.cuvee45: Cristal was first made in 1876 for Tsar Alexander the Second, and it is Louis Roederer's prestige cuvée. It is a vintage wine of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from the house's own Grand Cru vineyards. The clear, flat bottomed bottle is the Tsar's, and the cellophane keeps the light out. A quarter of the 2015 was made in oak casks, and it rests six to seven years in the cellar. Meyer lemon, white peach and fresh almond sit over chalk. I serve it at about nine degrees in a white wine glass, and leave the wrap on until I open it.
table.sale: Cristal, first made for the Tsar of Russia, comes only from Louis Roederer's own Grand Cru vineyards and only in ripe years. Shall I bring a bottle in its wrap?
table.cuvee10: Cristal is Louis Roederer's vintage prestige cuvée, first made for the Tsar in 1876, in a clear, flat bottomed bottle.
table.cuvee20: Louis Roederer first made Cristal in 1876, a vintage cuvée for the court of Tsar Alexander the Second. It comes only from the house's own Grand Cru vineyards, Pinot Noir with Chardonnay, in a clear bottle wrapped against the light.

guests.q: Why is Cristal in a clear bottle?
guests.a: The Tsar asked for clear glass with a flat base in 1876, so the story goes, so nothing could be hidden in it. The cellophane wrap keeps the light out.

guests.q: Is there a non vintage Cristal?
guests.a: No. Cristal is always a vintage wine, made only in years the house judges ripe enough; Collection is Roederer's multi vintage Brut.

guests.q: Is this the same as Roederer Estate from California?
guests.a: No. Cristal is made by Louis Roederer at Reims, from its own Grand Cru vineyards; Roederer Estate is a separate sparkling wine of California.

traps: Cristal is always vintage: there is no non vintage Cristal.
Cristal is Louis Roederer's cuvée from Reims, not the wine of Roederer Estate in California.
The clear bottle dates from the Tsar's order of 1876; the cellophane wrap is there to keep the light out.
Louis Roederer took a majority of Deutz in 1993, but Amour de Deutz is Deutz's own prestige cuvée, made at Aÿ, not a form of Cristal.

sheet.label: Cristal, Louis Roederer
sheet.note: The sheet and the label agree: Cristal, the name of the clear glass, with the vintage on the label because it is always a vintage wine.

questions.q: A guest asks for the prestige cuvée first made in 1876 for the court of Tsar Alexander II. Which house do you name?
questions.exp: Cristal is Louis Roederer's, first made for the Tsar in clear glass. Moët & Chandon makes Dom Pérignon, Pol Roger makes Sir Winston Churchill and Perrier-Jouët makes Belle Epoque.

questions.q: What sets Louis Roederer apart among the large houses, as the library teaches?
opts: It farms an unusually high share of its own fruit
It ferments every wine in small old oak casks
It blends three vintages for its prestige cuvée
It makes only Blanc de Blancs
questions.exp: Roederer farms much of its own fruit and makes Cristal from its own vineyards alone. Small old casks for every wine are Krug's mark, and three blended vintages are Laurent-Perrier's Grand Siècle.

questions.q: Which was the first Cristal made wholly from biodynamically farmed vines?
questions.exp: Cristal 2012, released in 2019, was the first from vines farmed biodynamically throughout, by the trade press. The 2008 and 2002 came before that change, and the 2015 after it.

report: Built on the published flagships record (codex58, key louis-roederer, refuted on 12 November 2026) and the library's p-louis-roederer and w-cristal: the story, the villages, the glass, the serving line and the three traps keep the published wording.

In tension with the published record, for the integrator to see: it leaves out the first sale to the public in 1945 as resting on one account; this record states it, with Wikipedia's Cristal page and a second account (Vinepair) found, and names the year as a sale, not as a vintage.

Refinements by the house's Cristal 2015 sheet and press file: six to seven years on lattes and six to twelve months after disgorging, where the published record says about six years and eight months; a quarter in oak; malolactic blocked; 7 grams a litre; 45 plots in seven crus; about three fifths Pinot Noir, given for that year only, as the published refuter asked.

The widow who led the house from 1932, and her husband, are described and not named: her dates were not found, and her start is 1932 by the house's press file and one account, 1933 by another; the house gives 43 years, the record more than forty.
Her grandson, who took over in the 1970s (1975 by one account), is living and not named.
Louis Roederer himself carries no dates, as in the published record, because accounts give 1798 and 1809 for his birth.
The sixty per cent of Deutz on 5 July 1993 is the Union des Maisons de Champagne's, as the Deutz record of chunk h2 tells it.
Cristal 2012 as the first from biodynamically farmed vines throughout is in The Drinks Business, Quill and Pad and Berry Bros; the certification of the whole estate came later and is left out.

Cristal Vinothèque: the house's sheet for the 1995 gives some twenty years in its cellars; the split between lattes and time after disgorging differs by account (ten and ten in one report, eight on lattes, six on points and eight after disgorging in another), so the record gives only the whole; the 2002 Late Release, a separate tier, is left out of forms.

style.reserve is empty: no house page read gives Collection's reserve figure (a critic's third of a perpetual reserve was not followed); Collection 242 as the first and as Brut Premier's successor is Jancis Robinson's and Tatler Asia's.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the library calls Roederer a house among the grandes marques, and a refuter should read a label.
The aged glass adds the house's own note on the 2008 Late Release to the published ageing line; a living name met in the research is added to people.json.
